question:
What is the area of the shaded pinwheel shown in the \(5 \times 5\) grid?

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The unshaded pieces have convenient bases along the grid's boundary, so subtract their areas from the whole square. Let \(P\) be the point where the four blades meet.

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

The white region consists of four \(1\times1\) corner squares and four triangles, one along each side of the grid. These pieces have disjoint interiors and cover all the unshaded area.

The top and bottom white triangles each have base \(3\), since a unit corner square occupies each end of the corresponding side. Their perpendicular heights, measured from \(P\), add to \(5\), the distance between the top and bottom sides. Their combined area is therefore
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot5=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
The left and right triangles likewise have bases \(3\) and heights adding to \(5\), so their combined area is also \(\frac{15}{2}\). This pairing avoids needing the exact location of \(P\).

The whole grid has area \(25\), and the four corner squares have total area \(4\). Hence the shaded area is
\[
25-4-\frac{15}{2}-\frac{15}{2}=\boxed{6}
\]
square units, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
